uncited: **Inputs:** A set of $n+1$ calibrated input images $I_0, \dots, I_n$, camera parameters (position, focal angles), and a 3D volume subdivision into layers.
**Outputs:** A set of colored voxels $S$ representing the reconstructed scene.
**Voxel Grid:** The 3D space is subdivided into layers of voxels at uniform distance $d$ from the camera.
**Time Complexity:** The algorithm iterates through all voxels in all layers and all input images.
For each voxel, it computes footprints and consistency metrics.
Exact visibility computation (via IB/LDI or ray casting) adds overhead compared to approximate methods.
**Memory Complexity:** Depends on the visibility structure.
**When to use:** When high geometric and photometric consistency is required and computational resources are sufficient.
When exact visibility is critical for quality.
**When not to use:** For real-time applications or very large scenes where memory is constrained (prefer IB over LDI, or approximate methods).
